recipes.name: Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
instructions: Dice the bacon and render in a large heavy pot over medium heat until crispy.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add pork shoulder cubes and brown on all sides.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add sauerkraut, sliced kielbasa, bay leaves, and allspice berries.
Pour in red wine and enough water to just cover the ingredients.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with rye bread.

geneticRelevance.note: Fermented cabbage provides glucosinolates that support detox pathways.
Contains pork and sausage — monitor if you have high saturated fat sensitivity.
Pork provides heme iron for efficient absorption.

recipes.culturalContext: Poland's national dish, traditionally prepared for holidays and hunting season. Each family has their own recipe, often improved by reheating over several days.

recipes.name: Borscht (Beet Soup)
instructions: In a large pot, sauté onion and carrot in a little oil until softened.
Add grated beets and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in stock and bring to a boil. Add potatoes.
Simmer for 40 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Add garlic and vinegar, cook 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

geneticRelevance.note: Beets are an excellent source of natural folate for methylation support.
Beets contain iron; vitamin C from the lemon juice enhances absorption.
Traditionally served with sour cream — suits those with dairy tolerance.

recipes.culturalContext: A cornerstone of Eastern European cuisine found across Ukraine, Russia, and Poland. Each region has distinct variations — some served hot, some cold.

recipes.name: Pierogi (Stuffed Dumplings)
instructions: Mix flour, egg, water, and salt into a smooth dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Combine mashed potatoes, cheese, and half the fried onion for filling.
Roll dough thin and cut circles with a glass.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold and seal edges firmly.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, about 3-4 minutes.
Pan-fry in butter until golden. Serve with remaining fried onion and sour cream.

geneticRelevance.note: Potato and wheat dough — benefits from strong AMY1 starch digestion.
Cheese filling and sour cream require good dairy tolerance.
Contains wheat — avoid if celiac risk is elevated.

nutritionalHighlights: Good energy source from complex carbs
recipes.culturalContext: Beloved across Poland, Ukraine, and neighboring countries. Pierogi are served at celebrations, holidays, and as everyday comfort food.

recipes.name: Dark Rye Bread with Kvass
instructions: Mix rye flour, bread flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Add sourdough starter, warm water, and molasses. Mix until combined.
Fold in caraway seeds. The dough will be sticky — this is normal for rye.
Shape into a loaf and place in a greased loaf pan. Cover and let rise 2-3 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Bake for 50 minutes until the crust is dark and firm.
Let cool completely before slicing. Best served with butter or alongside borscht.

geneticRelevance.note: Rye bread is lower glycemic than wheat — good for varied starch metabolism.
Contains gluten from rye and wheat — not suitable for celiac risk.
Fermented sourdough process produces beneficial compounds for gut health.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in B vitamins and minerals
recipes.culturalContext: Dark rye bread is a staple across Eastern Europe, particularly in the Baltics and Russia. Sourdough fermentation was the traditional leavening method for centuries.

recipes.name: Horiatiki (Greek Village Salad)
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, and onion in a large bowl.
Place the feta block on top — do not crumble it.
Add olives and season with oregano and salt.
Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

geneticRelevance.note: Feta cheese is lower in lactose than fresh dairy — often tolerated even with reduced lactase.
Olive oil provides monounsaturated fats that benefit cardiovascular health.
Olive oil and olives may support healthy HDL cholesterol levels.

nutritionalHighlights: High in antioxidants from tomatoes and olive oil
recipes.culturalContext: The authentic Greek salad never contains lettuce. It showcases the quality of simple ingredients — ripe tomatoes, quality olive oil, and real feta.

recipes.name: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan. Brown chicken pieces and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant. Add grated tomato and cook down.
Add paprika and saffron, stir for 30 seconds.
Return chicken, add rice, and stir to coat in the sofrito.
Pour in hot stock. Distribute rice evenly — do not stir from this point.
Cook on medium-high for 10 minutes, then reduce heat for 8 minutes.
Nestle seafood into the rice. Cook until mussels open and shrimp are pink.
Let rest 5 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice-based dish — benefits from good AMY1 starch digestion capacity.
Seafood provides omega-3 fatty acids; your FADS metabolism affects conversion.
Shellfish provides heme iron and zinc.

recipes.culturalContext: Originating in Valencia, Spain, paella is a celebratory dish traditionally cooked outdoors over wood fire. The prized socarrat is the crispy rice at the bottom.

recipes.name: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan. Sauté onion until translucent.
Add peppers and cook 5 minutes. Add eggplant and zucchini.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes, garlic, and herbs. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Adjust seasoning and finish with fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

geneticRelevance.note: Rich in beta-carotene from peppers — your BCO1 gene affects vitamin A conversion.
Olive oil base is ideal for those with elevated saturated fat sensitivity.
Tomatoes and peppers provide lycopene and other antioxidants.

recipes.culturalContext: A Provençal vegetable stew from Nice, France. Originally a humble peasant dish, it celebrates the summer harvest of southern France.

recipes.name: Pasta Puttanesca
instructions: Cook spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil and gently cook garlic and anchovies until anchovies dissolve.
Add chili flakes, olives, and capers. Cook 1 minute.
Add canned tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Toss drained pasta into the sauce with fresh parsley.
Serve immediately — no cheese needed.

geneticRelevance.note: Wheat pasta benefits from efficient starch digestion via AMY1.
Wheat-based — consider gluten-free pasta if celiac risk is elevated.
Anchovies provide omega-3s; olive oil provides monounsaturated fats.

nutritionalHighlights: Healthy fats from olive oil and fish
recipes.culturalContext: A classic Neapolitan pasta said to have originated as a quick pantry meal. The bold, briny flavors make it distinctly southern Italian.

recipes.name: Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
instructions: Soak wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer — do not boil.
Add tofu cubes and wakame. Heat through for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Dissolve miso paste into the broth through a strainer.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

geneticRelevance.note: Wakame seaweed contains omega-3 ALA; dashi provides iodine.
Fermented miso supports gut microbiome diversity.
Miso is high in sodium — reduce amount if salt-sensitive.

recipes.culturalContext: Miso soup is served with nearly every Japanese meal, particularly breakfast. The quality of dashi (kelp and bonito stock) is considered essential.

recipes.name: Salmon Teriyaki with Rice
ingredients: Sesame seeds and green onion for garnish
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar to make teriyaki sauce.
Pat salmon dry and cook skin-side down in an oiled pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes.
Flip salmon and pour teriyaki sauce into the pan.
Cook 3-4 minutes, spooning sauce over the fish as it thickens.
Serve over steamed rice, drizzled with sauce. Top with sesame seeds and green onion.

geneticRelevance.note: Salmon is one of the richest sources of EPA and DHA omega-3 fatty acids.
Salmon provides significant vitamin D — important if synthesis is reduced.
Served with white rice — higher glycemic, but traditional pairing.

nutritionalHighlights: Excellent omega-3 DHA and EPA source
Rich in vitamin D and B12
recipes.culturalContext: Teriyaki is a traditional Japanese cooking technique where food is glazed with a soy-mirin sauce. Home-style Japanese cooking emphasizes simple preparation of quality fish.

recipes.name: Natto over Rice
instructions: Stir natto vigorously with chopsticks until very stringy (about 50 stirs).
Add the included sauce packet, soy sauce, and mustard. Mix well.
Place over hot steamed rice.
Top with egg yolk, green onion, and nori if desired.

geneticRelevance.note: Fermented soy provides probiotics and isoflavones that support detox pathways.
White rice base — benefits from good AMY1 copy number.
Natto is one of the few plant sources containing vitamin K2 and some B12.

nutritionalHighlights: Very high in vitamin K2 (for bone health)
recipes.culturalContext: Natto is a traditional Japanese breakfast food, especially popular in eastern Japan. The strong flavor and sticky texture are an acquired taste but highly valued for health.

recipes.name: Saba Shioyake (Salt-Grilled Mackerel)
instructions: Salt mackerel fillets generously and let rest 20 minutes.
Pat dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
Grill or broil skin-side up for 5-6 minutes until skin is crispy and blistered.
Flip and cook 3-4 more minutes until cooked through.
Serve with grated daikon, a squeeze of lemon, and steamed rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Mackerel is extremely rich in omega-3 EPA and DHA.
One of the highest dietary vitamin D sources.
Salt-curing method adds sodium — adjust if salt-sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: One of the richest fish in omega-3s
recipes.culturalContext: Saba shioyake is a classic Japanese home meal — simple salt and fire bring out the rich flavor of mackerel. A staple of the traditional ichiju-sansai (one soup, three sides) meal format.

recipes.name: Sambar (Lentil Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Cook toor dal with turmeric until soft and mushy. Mash and set aside.
Boil vegetables in water until tender.
Soak tamarind in warm water and extract the pulp.
Combine dal, vegetables, tamarind water, and sambar powder. Simmer 10 minutes.
In a small pan, heat coconut oil. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and dried chilies.
When mustard seeds pop, pour the tempering over the sambar. Serve with rice or idli.

geneticRelevance.note: Lentil and rice pairing provides complete protein with complex carbohydrates.
Lentils are an excellent natural source of folate.
Lentils provide plant-based iron; tamarind's vitamin C aids absorption.

recipes.culturalContext: Sambar is the daily staple of South Indian cuisine, served with rice, idli, dosa, or vada. Every household has its own sambar powder blend.

recipes.name: Masala Dosa with Coconut Chutney
instructions: Grind soaked rice and dal into a smooth batter. Ferment overnight.
For filling: temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil, add onion and turmeric.
Add mashed potatoes, mix well and season.
For chutney: blend coconut, green chilies, and ginger with water.
Heat a flat pan, spread a ladleful of batter in a thin circle.
Drizzle oil around edges. When crispy, add potato filling and fold.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice and potato-based — fermentation partially breaks down starches.
Fermented batter provides probiotics beneficial for gut health.
Fenugreek has bitter compounds — perception varies by TAS2R38 genotype.

nutritionalHighlights: Good source of B vitamins from fermentation
recipes.culturalContext: Dosa is a beloved South Indian breakfast and snack. The fermentation process was developed centuries ago, naturally improving nutrition and digestibility.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani (Black Lentil Curry)
ingredients: 1 cup whole black urad dal, soaked overnight
1 tsp each: cumin, coriander, garam masala
instructions: Pressure cook soaked dal and rajma until very soft (about 30 minutes).
In a heavy pot, melt butter and sauté onion until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic, cook 2 minutes. Add tomato puree and spices.
Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Add the cooked lentils with their water. Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Stir in cream, adjust salt. The dal should be rich and creamy. Serve with naan or rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Black lentils are exceptionally rich in natural folate.
Contains butter and cream — suits those with dairy tolerance.
Rich dish with butter and cream — moderate portions if fat-sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Very high in protein and fiber
Iron and B vitamins from lentils
recipes.culturalContext: Dal Makhani originated in Punjabi cuisine and became famous through Mughlai-influenced restaurant cooking. Slow cooking is the secret to its creamy texture.

recipes.name: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: Lemon wedges and onion rings for serving
instructions: Make deep slashes in chicken pieces for marinade penetration.
Mix yogurt, tandoori masala, ginger-garlic paste, chili, turmeric, lemon, oil, and salt.
Coat chicken thoroughly and marinate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to maximum (250°C) or prepare a grill.
Cook chicken for 20-25 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges, onion rings, and mint chutney.

geneticRelevance.note: Yogurt marinade tenderizes the meat — requires dairy tolerance.
Dark meat chicken provides good heme iron.
Turmeric and spice blend contain bitter compounds — perception varies.

recipes.culturalContext: Tandoori cooking dates back thousands of years in the Indian subcontinent. The intense heat of the clay tandoor oven creates the characteristic char and smoky flavor.

recipes.name: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Blend fresh tomatoes and red peppers into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Fry onion until golden.
Add tomato paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the blended tomato-pepper mixture. Cook on medium heat until reduced and oil floats on top.
Add seasonings, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and whole scotch bonnet.
Add washed rice and enough water to just cover. Stir once.
Cover tightly with foil then lid. Cook on low heat for 30 minutes without opening.
Fluff with a fork. Serve with fried plantain and grilled chicken.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice-based dish — amylase efficiency affects how well you digest the starches.
Rich in beta-carotene from tomatoes and red peppers.
White rice is higher glycemic — pair with protein and vegetables.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in lycopene from tomato base
recipes.culturalContext: Jollof rice is the crown jewel of West African cuisine, with a friendly rivalry between Nigeria and Ghana over who makes it best. Essential at every celebration.

recipes.name: Egusi Soup
instructions: Cook assorted meats with onion and seasoning until tender. Reserve stock.
Heat palm oil in a pot (do not bleach). Add chopped onion and fry.
Add blended tomatoes and peppers. Cook until reduced.
Mix ground egusi with a little water to form a paste. Add to the pot in lumps.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes, then stir to break up lumps.
Add meat stock, cooked meats, and crayfish. Simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped greens and cook 5 more minutes. Serve with pounded yam or fufu.

geneticRelevance.note: Red meat and organ meats provide highly bioavailable heme iron.
Bitter leaf and spinach are excellent sources of natural folate.
Palm oil is high in saturated fat — consider moderation if sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Melon seeds are rich in protein and healthy fats
Leafy greens provide iron and folate
Palm oil contains vitamin E tocotrienols
recipes.culturalContext: Egusi soup is a beloved dish across Nigeria and West Africa. The melon seeds give it a distinctive nutty, thickened texture unlike any other cuisine.

recipes.name: Groundnut Soup (Peanut Stew)
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in oil. Set aside.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add blended tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook 10 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter until smooth.
Add chicken stock gradually, stirring to prevent lumps.
Return chicken, add whole scotch bonnet. Simmer 35 minutes.
The soup should be thick and rich. Serve over rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Peanuts contain mostly monounsaturated fats — generally well-tolerated.
Peanuts are a good source of folate.
Chicken provides B12 for methylation support.

nutritionalHighlights: High protein from peanuts and chicken
Good source of niacin and folate
recipes.culturalContext: Groundnut soup is found across West Africa from Senegal to Nigeria. The peanut was brought from the Americas but became deeply integrated into African cuisine.

recipes.name: Fufu with Light Soup
instructions: Cook meat with onion and seasoning until tender. Reserve the stock.
Add blended tomatoes, peppers, and ginger to the stock. Boil for 20 minutes.
Add garden eggs or okra. Simmer until vegetables are tender.
For fufu: boil water in a pot, gradually add cassava flour while stirring vigorously.
Keep stirring until the fufu is smooth and pulls away from the pot sides.
Shape fufu into balls. Serve with the light soup and meat.

geneticRelevance.note: Cassava/plantain fufu is very starchy — AMY1 copy number affects digestion efficiency.
High glycemic starch — balance with the protein-rich soup.
Goat meat provides bioavailable heme iron.

recipes.culturalContext: Fufu is the quintessential West African staple, eaten by hand with soup. The art of pounding fufu is a cultural tradition, though modern flour makes it easier.

recipes.name: Coq au Vin
instructions: Marinate chicken in wine overnight (optional but recommended).
Pat chicken dry and brown in butter. Set aside.
Cook bacon lardons until crispy. Add pearl onions and mushrooms.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir. Cook 2 minutes.
Return chicken, pour in wine, add herbs, garlic, and seasonings.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until chicken is very tender.
Remove herbs. Serve with crusty bread or mashed potatoes.

geneticRelevance.note: Cooked wine retains some alcohol — relevant if ALDH2 metabolism is slow.
Chicken thigh meat provides moderate heme iron.
Contains butter and bacon — monitor saturated fat intake if sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Mushrooms provide vitamin D and selenium
recipes.culturalContext: A classic French country dish from Burgundy. Originally made with an old rooster (coq), the long braise in wine tenderized tough meat — a hallmark of peasant ingenuity.

recipes.name: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, cut into thick chips
Lemon wedges and mushy peas for serving
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick chips. Soak in cold water 30 minutes, then dry thoroughly.
Fry chips at 150°C for 8 minutes to cook through. Drain and set aside.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt. Whisk in cold beer until smooth.
Pat fish dry and dust lightly with flour.
Dip fish in batter and fry at 180°C for 5-6 minutes until golden and crispy.
Re-fry chips at 190°C for 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper. Serve with salt, malt vinegar, lemon, and mushy peas.

geneticRelevance.note: Cod and haddock provide lean protein and some omega-3 fatty acids.
Potato chips are high in starch — AMY1 affects digestion efficiency.
Deep frying adds fat — baked version is an alternative for fat-sensitive individuals.

nutritionalHighlights: Good source of lean protein from white fish
Potatoes provide vitamin C and potassium
recipes.culturalContext: Britain's iconic takeaway, fish and chips became popular in the 1860s as affordable protein for the working class. Traditionally wrapped in newspaper and eaten by the seaside.

recipes.name: Irish Lamb Stew
instructions: Layer lamb, potatoes, carrots, and onions in a heavy pot.
Add herbs, bay leaves, and season with salt and pepper.
Pour in stock to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very gentle simmer.
Cover and cook for 2 hours until lamb is fall-apart tender.
Remove bay leaves. Serve in deep bowls with crusty soda bread.

geneticRelevance.note: Lamb is rich in heme iron and zinc — excellent for iron metabolism.
Potatoes provide the starchy base of this hearty stew.
Lamb contains saturated fat — trim excess if sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Excellent source of iron and zinc from lamb
Root vegetables provide fiber and vitamins
recipes.culturalContext: Irish stew is one of the oldest and most iconic dishes of Ireland. Originally made with mutton (older sheep) and root vegetables available through harsh winters.

recipes.name: Colcannon (Potato and Cabbage Mash)
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain and mash.
Meanwhile, cook shredded cabbage in boiling water for 3-4 minutes. Drain well.
Heat milk and half the butter together.
Fold hot milk mixture and cabbage into mashed potatoes.
Season with salt, pepper, and green onions.
Serve with a well of melted butter in the center.

geneticRelevance.note: Cabbage and kale provide glucosinolates supporting detox enzyme function.
Contains milk and butter — suits those with dairy tolerance.
Potato-based — benefits from good AMY1 starch digestion.

nutritionalHighlights: Vitamin C from potatoes and cabbage
recipes.culturalContext: A traditional Irish and Scottish dish, colcannon is associated with Halloween when charms were hidden in the mash for divination. Simple ingredients elevated by good butter.

recipes.name: Tamales de Pollo (Chicken Tamales)
ingredients: 2 cups salsa verde or red salsa
instructions: Soak corn husks in warm water for at least 1 hour.
Beat lard until fluffy. Gradually add masa harina, broth, baking powder, and salt.
Beat until a small ball of dough floats in water (means it's light enough).
Mix shredded chicken with salsa.
Spread a thin layer of masa on a corn husk. Add chicken filling.
Fold the sides and bottom of the husk to enclose the tamale.
Stand tamales upright in a steamer. Steam for 90 minutes.
Tamales are done when the dough pulls away cleanly from the husk.

geneticRelevance.note: Masa (nixtamalized corn) is a traditional starch — AMY1 efficiency matters.
Traditional lard in masa — substitute vegetable oil if fat-sensitive.
Salsa verde with tomatillos provides vitamin C and antioxidants.

nutritionalHighlights: Balanced protein from chicken and corn
recipes.culturalContext: Tamales date back to the Aztec and Maya civilizations, served as portable food for travelers and warriors. Making tamales is still a communal family event across Mexico.

recipes.name: Mole Negro
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry pan until fragrant. Soak in hot water 30 minutes.
Toast sesame and pumpkin seeds. Toast the stale tortilla until dark.
Blend soaked chiles with roasted tomatoes, onion, and garlic.
Add seeds, tortilla, spices, and chocolate. Blend until smooth.
Cook the sauce in oil for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add chicken stock gradually until desired consistency. Simmer 45 minutes.
Season with salt and a pinch of sugar to balance the bitterness.
Serve over turkey, chicken, or enchiladas.

geneticRelevance.note: Dark chocolate and charred chiles have bitter compounds — TAS2R38 genotype affects perception.
Dark chocolate contains theobromine, metabolized similarly to caffeine.
Chiles, chocolate, and seeds provide a wealth of antioxidants.

nutritionalHighlights: Pumpkin seeds provide zinc and magnesium
recipes.culturalContext: Mole is considered the pinnacle of Mexican cuisine, originating in Oaxaca and Puebla. Some moles contain over 30 ingredients and take days to prepare.

recipes.name: Pozole Rojo (Red Hominy Stew)
ingredients: Shredded cabbage, radishes, lime, oregano for toppings
instructions: Simmer pork in salted water for 90 minutes until tender. Skim foam.
Toast dried chiles and soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend soaked chiles with garlic, onion, and a cup of pork broth.
Strain chile sauce into the pork broth. Add hominy.
Simmer 30 minutes more. Season with oregano and salt.
Serve in deep bowls with shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, lime, and oregano on the side.

geneticRelevance.note: Hominy (nixtamalized corn) is a traditional Mesoamerican starch.
Pork provides heme iron in this protein-rich soup.
Dried chiles are rich in carotenoids and vitamin A precursors.

nutritionalHighlights: Fresh toppings add vitamins C and K
recipes.culturalContext: Pozole has pre-Columbian origins and was an Aztec ceremonial dish. Today it's served at celebrations, holidays, and as a hangover remedy across Mexico.

recipes.name: Sopa de Frijol Negro (Black Bean Soup)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black beans, soaked overnight
Lime juice, crema, and cilantro for serving
instructions: Drain soaked beans and place in a large pot with fresh water or stock.
Add onion half, garlic, epazote, and chipotle. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 60-90 minutes until beans are very tender.
Remove epazote and chipotle. Blend half the soup and return to the pot.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Serve topped with crema, cilantro, and a lime wedge.

geneticRelevance.note: Black beans are one of the richest sources of natural folate.
Beans contain resistant starch that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.
Beans have a low glycemic index, helping stabilize blood sugar.

nutritionalHighlights: Extremely high in folate and fiber
Low glycemic for blood sugar management
recipes.culturalContext: Black beans are a Mesoamerican staple cultivated for over 7,000 years. Combined with corn, they form a complete protein — the foundation of the traditional diet.

recipes.name: Gravlax (Cured Salmon)
ingredients: Crispbread and mustard-dill sauce for serving
instructions: Mix salt, sugar, and pepper together.
Place half the dill in a dish. Lay salmon skin-side down on the dill.
Rub the salt-sugar mixture over the flesh. Drizzle with aquavit.
Cover with remaining dill. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap.
Place a weight on top and refrigerate for 48-72 hours, turning once daily.
Scrape off the cure and dill. Slice thinly on the diagonal.
Serve on crispbread with mustard-dill sauce.

geneticRelevance.note: Salmon is rich in omega-3 EPA and DHA — your FADS genes affect how you utilize these.
Salmon is one of the best dietary vitamin D sources — crucial in low-sunlight Nordic climates.
Salt-cured — rinse or reduce cure if salt-sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in vitamin D and B12
High-quality protein with no cooking required
recipes.culturalContext: Gravlax means 'buried salmon' in Scandinavian — originally salmon was cured by burying it in sand above the tide line. Today it's a beloved Nordic appetizer and holiday tradition.

recipes.name: Smørrebrød (Open-Faced Sandwiches)
instructions: Spread rye bread generously with butter.
Layer smoked fish on the bread.
Top with sliced egg, pickled onion, capers, and dill.
Add a dollop of remoulade sauce.
Garnish with radish slices. Eat with knife and fork.

geneticRelevance.note: Smoked herring and mackerel are extremely rich in omega-3 fatty acids.
Fatty fish compensates for limited sunlight in Nordic latitudes.
Rye bread contains gluten — use gluten-free bread if celiac risk is elevated.

nutritionalHighlights: Dense nutrition from rye, fish, and eggs
recipes.culturalContext: Smørrebrød is Denmark's iconic lunch tradition, elevated to an art form. The open sandwich must be assembled and eaten in order — never picked up by hand.

recipes.name: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Soak breadcrumbs in milk. Mix with meat, egg, onion, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Roll into small, even balls (about 2cm diameter).
Brown meatballs in butter in batches. Set aside.
Deglaze pan with beef stock, scraping up brown bits.
Stir in cream and simmer until sauce thickens.
Return meatballs to sauce. Simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with mashed potatoes, lingonberry jam, and pickled cucumber.

geneticRelevance.note: Cream sauce and milk require good dairy tolerance — Nordic populations have high lactase persistence.
Beef provides heme iron and zinc.
Cream-based sauce — use lighter version if saturated fat sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Good protein and iron from beef
recipes.culturalContext: Swedish meatballs have been a staple since the 18th century, possibly influenced by Turkish kofta. The lingonberry accompaniment is essential and non-negotiable.

recipes.name: Lohikeitto (Finnish Salmon Soup)
instructions: Melt butter in a pot. Add leek and carrot, cook until softened.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a boil and cook until potatoes are almost tender.
Add salmon cubes and allspice. Cook gently for 5 minutes — do not boil.
Stir in cream and heat through.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Serve garnished with generous fresh dill.

geneticRelevance.note: Fresh salmon provides high levels of omega-3 EPA and DHA.
Salmon is a critical vitamin D source for high-latitude populations.
Cream-based broth requires good lactase persistence — common in Nordic ancestry.

nutritionalHighlights: Excellent omega-3 and vitamin D source
Balanced meal with protein, carbs, and healthy fats
recipes.culturalContext: Lohikeitto is Finland's most beloved soup, considered the national dish by many Finns. It showcases the pure flavors of Finnish ingredients — salmon, potato, dill, and cream.

recipes.name: Hummus bil Tahini
ingredients: Paprika and fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Process chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin in a food processor.
Add reserved chickpea liquid or ice water gradually until very smooth and creamy.
Process for 3-5 minutes — longer blending gives silkier texture.
Season with salt. Spread on a plate with a well in the center.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Serve with warm pita bread.

geneticRelevance.note: Chickpeas are an excellent source of natural folate for methylation support.
Chickpeas contain complex carbs and resistant starch.
Tahini and chickpeas provide plant-based iron; lemon juice aids absorption.

nutritionalHighlights: Tahini provides calcium and healthy fats
recipes.culturalContext: Hummus is ancient — chickpeas have been cultivated in the Levant for over 10,000 years. The combination with tahini creates a complete protein, central to the regional diet.

recipes.name: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Toast or fry pita pieces until crispy and golden.
Combine all chopped vegetables and fresh herbs in a large bowl.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, sumac, and salt.
Pour dressing over salad and toss well.
Add crispy pita just before serving so it stays crunchy.

geneticRelevance.note: Tomatoes and herbs provide carotenoids and vitamin A precursors.
Sumac and fresh herbs are rich in polyphenol antioxidants.
Toasted pita adds crunch but also wheat starch.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in vitamin C from fresh vegetables
Light and refreshing with good fiber
recipes.culturalContext: Fattoush is a Levantine bread salad born from the resourcefulness of using stale bread. Sumac gives it the distinctive tangy flavor that defines the dish.

recipes.name: Shish Tawook (Chicken Kebab)
ingredients: Pita, garlic sauce, and pickled turnips for serving
instructions: Mix yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and all spices.
Marinate chicken cubes for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
Thread chicken onto skewers.
Grill over high heat for 12-15 minutes, turning regularly.
Serve in warm pita with garlic sauce (toum), pickled turnips, and fresh vegetables.

geneticRelevance.note: Yogurt marinade tenderizes chicken — lower lactose than fresh milk.
Chicken provides moderate amounts of heme iron and B vitamins.
Cumin and coriander have mild bitter notes — perception varies by genotype.

nutritionalHighlights: Yogurt marinade adds probiotics and calcium
recipes.culturalContext: Shish tawook is a staple of Levantine street food and home cooking. The yogurt-lemon marinade is what gives the chicken its characteristic tender, tangy flavor.

recipes.name: Mujaddara (Lentils and Rice with Onions)
instructions: Cook lentils in water until almost tender, about 20 minutes. Drain.
Slice onions thinly. Fry 2/3 of them in olive oil until very dark and crispy. Set aside.
In the same pot, sauté remaining onions until golden.
Add rice, lentils, cumin, salt, and 2 cups water.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until rice is done.
Fluff and serve topped with the crispy onions and a side of yogurt.

geneticRelevance.note: Lentils are among the richest food sources of natural folate.
Rice and lentils together — your AMY1 gene affects starch digestion efficiency.
Lentils provide plant-based iron; onions contain prebiotic fiber.

nutritionalHighlights: Complete plant protein from lentil-rice combination
Very high in folate and fiber
recipes.culturalContext: Mujaddara is mentioned in medieval Arab cookbooks and considered one of the world's oldest comfort foods. Despite its simplicity, the caramelized onions elevate it to something extraordinary.

recipes.name: Pad Thai
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water until pliable but still firm. Drain.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar for the sauce.
Stir-fry garlic and protein in a hot wok with oil until cooked. Push to side.
Crack eggs into the wok and scramble.
Add noodles and sauce. Toss everything together over high heat.
Add bean sprouts and green onions. Toss briefly.
Serve immediately with crushed peanuts, lime, and chili flakes.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice noodles are a traditional carbohydrate — AMY1 affects digestion efficiency.
Shrimp provide some omega-3s; peanuts add healthy monounsaturated fats.
Rice noodles have moderate glycemic impact — protein and fat in the dish help balance.

nutritionalHighlights: Tamarind provides vitamin C and antioxidants
recipes.culturalContext: Pad Thai was promoted as Thailand's national dish in the 1930s-40s to build national identity and reduce rice consumption. It brilliantly balances sweet, sour, salty, and savory.

recipes.name: Pho Bo (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: Fresh herbs: Thai basil, cilantro, mint
Bean sprouts, lime, chili, hoisin sauce
instructions: Blanch beef bones in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Char onion and ginger over open flame or under broiler.
Toast spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Combine bones, brisket, charred aromatics, and spices in a large pot with water.
Simmer for 3 hours, skimming occasionally. Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Strain broth. Slice brisket thinly.
Cook rice noodles. Assemble bowls with noodles, sliced beef, and hot broth.
Serve with fresh herbs, sprouts, lime, and chili.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice noodles are the base — traditional gluten-free carbohydrate.
Beef broth and meat are rich in heme iron and bone marrow nutrients.
Bone broth provides collagen and minerals; fresh herbs add antioxidants.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in collagen from bone broth
Fresh herbs provide vitamins and antioxidants
recipes.culturalContext: Pho emerged in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century, likely influenced by French and Chinese cooking. The broth is everything — a great pho is judged by its clarity and depth of flavor.

recipes.name: Thai Green Curry (Gaeng Khiao Wan)
instructions: Heat the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk in a wok.
Add curry paste and fry until fragrant and oil separates.
Add chicken and cook until sealed on the outside.
Pour in remaining coconut milk, add eggplant and lime leaves.
Simmer 15 minutes until chicken is cooked and eggplant is tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Stir in Thai basil.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Coconut milk is high in saturated fat — use light version if sensitive.
Served with jasmine rice — traditional starch pairing.
Thai basil and eggplant contain bitter compounds — TAS2R38 affects perception.

recipes.culturalContext: Thai curries are defined by their paste — a hand-pounded blend of fresh herbs and spices. Green curry is the hottest of the three main Thai curries (red, green, yellow).

recipes.name: Larb (Thai Meat Salad)
instructions: Cook ground meat in a dry pan, breaking up lumps. Let cool slightly.
Make toasted rice powder by dry-roasting rice grains and grinding.
Toss meat with lime juice, fish sauce, shallots, herbs, chili, and rice powder.
Serve in lettuce cups with sticky rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Ground meat provides bioavailable heme iron.
Toasted rice powder adds texture and carbohydrates.
Fresh herbs and lime create complex flavor — perception varies by genotype.

nutritionalHighlights: Fresh herbs add vitamins and antioxidants
recipes.culturalContext: Larb is the national dish of Laos and beloved across Thailand's Isan region. The toasted rice powder gives it a distinctive nutty crunch and is considered essential.

recipes.name: Congee (Rice Porridge) with Century Egg
instructions: Rinse rice and add to a large pot with water or stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cook for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice breaks down into porridge.
Season pork mince with soy sauce. Stir into the congee in small clumps.
Cook 5 more minutes until pork is done.
Fold in chopped century egg. Season with sesame oil and white pepper.
Serve topped with green onions, fried shallots, and ginger.

geneticRelevance.note: Long-cooked rice breaks down starches for easier digestion.
Congee is a traditional comfort food — gentle on digestion if ALDH2 metabolism affects tolerance.
Pork and century egg provide protein and iron.

nutritionalHighlights: Century egg is rich in iron and amino acids
recipes.culturalContext: Congee has been a Chinese staple for thousands of years, valued as comfort food and medicine food. In Cantonese culture, the silky texture of well-made congee is a point of pride.

recipes.name: Siu Mai (Pork and Shrimp Dumplings)
ingredients: 3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
Green peas or crab roe for topping
instructions: Mix pork, shrimp, mushrooms, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, pepper, and cornstarch.
Stir vigorously in one direction until mixture is sticky and bouncy.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of a wonton wrapper.
Gather the wrapper around the filling, leaving the top open.
Top each with a green pea or dot of crab roe.
Steam in a bamboo steamer for 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Serve immediately with chili oil and soy sauce.

geneticRelevance.note: Wheat wrappers add some starch — mostly protein-focused dish.
Shrimp provide omega-3s and selenium.
Pork provides heme iron; shiitake mushrooms add vitamin D.

nutritionalHighlights: High protein from pork and shrimp
Steaming preserves nutrients without added fat
Mushrooms provide vitamin D and B vitamins
recipes.culturalContext: Siu mai is a cornerstone of Cantonese dim sum culture, where tea and small dishes are shared among family and friends in a ritual called yum cha (drinking tea).

recipes.name: Jiaozi (Chinese Dumplings)
ingredients: 2 cups napa cabbage, finely chopped and squeezed dry
Black vinegar and chili oil for dipping
instructions: Mix flour with boiling water. Knead into a smooth dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix pork with cabbage, green onions, soy sauce, sesame oil, and ginger.
Roll dough into a rope, cut into pieces, and roll each into a thin circle.
Place filling in center, fold and pleat the edge to seal.
Boil in water until they float plus 2 more minutes, OR pan-fry for potstickers.
Serve with black vinegar and chili oil for dipping.

geneticRelevance.note: Wheat dough wrapper — northern Chinese cuisine is wheat-based.
Napa cabbage provides glucosinolates for detox enzyme support.
Wheat-based — consider rice paper wrappers if celiac risk is elevated.

recipes.culturalContext: Jiaozi are the most important food of Chinese New Year, symbolizing wealth (they resemble gold ingots). Making dumplings together is a cherished family bonding activity.

recipes.name: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)
instructions: Prepare each vegetable separately: blanch spinach and sprouts, sauté carrot and zucchini.
Season each vegetable lightly with sesame oil, soy sauce, and sesame seeds.
Cook bulgogi beef in a hot pan.
Fry eggs sunny-side up.
Arrange rice in bowls. Place vegetables and beef in sections on top.
Top with fried egg and a generous spoonful of gochujang.
Mix everything together before eating.

geneticRelevance.note: Rice base — a Korean dietary staple dependent on AMY1 efficiency.
Beef and spinach both provide iron — heme and non-heme sources.
Spinach and bean sprouts provide natural folate.

nutritionalHighlights: Extremely balanced meal with all food groups
Gochujang contains capsaicin with metabolism-boosting properties
recipes.culturalContext: Bibimbap means 'mixed rice' and embodies the Korean philosophy of balancing colors, flavors, and nutrients. Jeonju-style bibimbap is considered the most elaborate version.

recipes.name: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
instructions: Sauté pork belly until fat renders. Add kimchi and cook 5 minutes.
Add onion, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir well.
Pour in water or broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Add soft tofu carefully. Simmer 5 more minutes.
Top with green onions and serve bubbling hot with rice.

geneticRelevance.note: Fermented napa cabbage kimchi provides probiotics and glucosinolates.
Kimchi is high in sodium — reduce kimchi amount if salt-sensitive.
Pork belly adds saturated fat — use lean pork if sensitive.

nutritionalHighlights: Rich in probiotics from aged kimchi
High protein from pork and tofu
Capsaicin from chili has metabolic benefits
recipes.culturalContext: Kimchi jjigae is the ultimate Korean comfort food, best made with well-aged kimchi that's too sour to eat raw. It's the most commonly cooked dish in Korean homes.
